title: bibliolatam: Latin American Bibliographic Data Adapters for 'bibliometrix'
description:
bibliolatam is an open-source R package developed by the Brazilian Research Archive Network (BRAN Org) that bridges Latin American, Caribbean, and Iberian Diamond Open Access scientific repositories into mainstream bibliometric pipelines (bibliometrix, biblioshiny, VOSviewer, Gephi) and standalone data workflows.

Scientific Context & Motivation

Commercial citation indexes (Web of Science, Scopus) systematically under-represent scientific production from the Global South. In Latin America, regional science has historically flourished under publicly funded, non-commercial Diamond Open Access infrastructures (SciELO, Redalyc, SPELL) and national thesis/dissertation repositories (BDTD, Oasisbr, LA Referencia). Because mainstream scientometric packages restrict their native parsers to commercial Global North formats, regional research is often excluded from large-scale quantitative science studies. bibliolatam fills this structural gap by providing modular parsers, automated REST API clients, and entity resolution algorithms designed specifically for regional data semantics.

Supported Repositories & Data Coverage

  • SciELO (Scientific Electronic Library Online): Automated Crossref REST API querying (DOI prefix 10.1590), tabular CSV ingestion, and full-text NLM/JATS XML parsing with automated extraction of cited reference lists (<ref-list>) into standard WoS-format CR tags for co-citation and bibliographic coupling.
  • BDTD (Biblioteca Digital Brasileira de Teses e Dissertações): Automated VuFind REST API search across Brazilian graduate programs, degree filtering (theses vs. dissertations), local CSV/TSV ingestion, handle mapping to UT, and academic advisors mapped to RP.
  • Oasisbr (Portal Brasileiro de Publicações Científicas em Acesso Aberto): Multi-institutional Brazilian open science repository ingestion via VuFind REST API and tabular exports.
  • LA Referencia: Federated query engine connecting 12 Latin American national repository networks across South America, Central America, and Mexico.
  • Redalyc & AmeliCA: Ingestion of BibTeX, RIS, and CSV exports with dedicated parsing for Hispanic compound surnames.
  • SPELL / ANPAD: Ingestion of administration, accounting, and economics literature from Brazilian scientific associations.

Key Architectural Capabilities

  • Federated Omnisearch (omnisearch_bibliolatam): Query SciELO, BDTD, Oasisbr, and LA Referencia simultaneously with API-level publication year filtering and automated multi-source deduplication.
  • Entity Resolution & Deduplication (merge_bibliolatam): Combines heterogeneous datasets by canonical DOI cleaning and fuzzy title matching (Levenshtein distance), fusing complementary metadata tags.
  • Regional Author Normalization (normalize_authors): Vectorized engine handling Brazilian generational suffixes (Junior, Filho, Neto, Sobrinho), compound particles (da, de, do, del, van), and institutional authorship.
  • Strict S3 bibliometrixDB Contract: Guarantees full compliance with Web of Science tags (TI, AU, SO, PY, CR, DE, DI, C1, RP, SR, JI, J9) with zero metadata fabrication (missing fields populated as NA or 0).
  • Standalone Trilingual GUI (run_app): Self-contained Shiny dashboard supporting live runtime switching between English, Portuguese, and Spanish with 1-click CSV and .RData export.

Quick Start

# Install from GitHub
remotes::install_github("BRAN-Org/bibliolatam")

# Launch standalone GUI
bibliolatam::run_app()

# Programmatic Omnisearch across 4 regional databases:
library(bibliolatam)
df <- omnisearch_bibliolatam(
  query = "energia solar",
  sources = c("scielo", "bdtd", "oasisbr", "lareferencia"),
  years = c(2020, 2024),
  deduplicate = TRUE
)
